In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
elastin is a very long, very flexible, and extremely insoluble polypeptide, with a high content of hydrophobic amino acid residues and a low content of charged amino acid residues.

the primary structure of elastin is a unique combination of a high content of glycine and alanine residues, a high content of lysine residues, and the absence of cysteine, tryptophan, and methionine residues.
elastin is a highly repetitive protein, with a primary structure that is very similar to that of collagen.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the primary structure of elastin is a mosaic of repeating sequences of hydrophobic and lysine-containing domains, and that the repeating sequence of hydrophobic amino acids, which has a length of approximately 20 residues and which is interrupted by a lysine-containing domain, is the fundamental repeating unit of the elastin molecule.

the primary structures of elastins a and b differ from the primary structure of elastin c in that the former have an extra domain, the so-called variable region, located at the carboxyl end of the polypeptide chain.
elastin is a protein with a unique structure that is well adapted for its function as an extensible tissue component.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amino acid sequence of bovine elastins a, b, c is very similar to that of human elastin.
the amino acid sequence of tropoelastins from different species is highly conserved, with 98% of the residues being identical.
there is only one elastin gene in the human and the bovine genome.
